methodology_note: Supplemental health/life insurer (Aflac Japan + Aflac U.S.) — not an owner-FCF DCF. Operating/free cash flow for an insurer reflects premium float and investment-portfolio timing, not distributable owner earnings, and GAAP net income/EPS is dominated by non-economic investment mark-to-market noise (FY2025 net earnings fell to $3.6B from $5.4B in FY2024 on net investment losses and CECL allowances even as management's own adjusted EPS hit a record $7.49). Reported shareholders' equity (and therefore BVPS) is itself volatile because it carries AOCI — unrealized gains/losses on the large yen-denominated JGB and USD fixed-income portfolios swing with interest rates (BVPS fell from $46.86 FY2020 to $25.17 FY2021 as rates rose, pure AOCI mechanics, not a change in franchise value). This model follows the same book-value-compounding approach used elsewhere in this project for insurers/holdcos (FRFHF, and the residual-income variant for banks NAB.AX/IAG.AX/SRBK): (1) project BVPS per share forward at a scenario compounding rate that reflects retained earnings after the dividend and after buybacks made at about twice book (which reduce book per share), plus a modest allowance for rising ROE and reinvestment yields, (2) add back the dividend per share each year (management targets total per-share value creation, not book value net of the payout), (3) apply an exit price-to-book multiple anchored to the post-2022 (AOCI-stabilized) trading range of ~2.0-2.4x, and (4) discount dividends plus the Year-5 terminal value at a cost of equity (never WACC — there is no debt to add back and net debt is held at zero; this is a per-share equity-holder valuation, not an enterprise value).

inputs.notes: Model: BVPS compounding x exit P/B, dividends plus Year-5 terminal value discounted at cost of equity (insurer route per dcf-methods SKILL.md). UPDATE of the 2026-09-25 build, same model. net_debt held at 0: senior notes fund the portfolio backing policy liabilities and the flow is already post-financing. Anchor correction: the prior version divided equity by the WEIGHTED-AVERAGE share count (59.96 at Q2 2026, 55.13 at FY2025); the 10-Q/10-K report period-end BVPS of 59.08 (Q3 2026) and 56.85 (FY2025) and those are used here. Driver correction: the prior rationale treated the ~5-6%/yr buyback as a tailwind to BVPS; repurchases at ~2x book reduce book per share, which is why BVPS excluding AOCI has been flat through 2026. normalized_eps_estimate lowered 8.0 to 7.6: nine-month 2026 adjusted EPS was 5.92, flat on 2025, and Q3 included a $0.71 actuarial unlock. Price is a regular-session close, not an after-hours print.
inputs.share_count_basis: period-end common shares outstanding at 2026-09-30 per Q3 2026 10-Q (494.607M on the cover at 2026-10-27); held flat in the per-share model because buybacks act through the BVPS path, not a separate share projection
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity, not WACC: USD flows, ~4.5% US 10-year risk-free plus ~4.5-5.5% equity risk premium at a beta near 1.0 gives 9.0% base (8.5% bull, 10.0% bear). Unchanged from the prior version.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: average of base bvps_growth_rates; capital arithmetic (ROE less dividend less buybacks above book) plus observed 2026 run rate, not the AOCI-driven historical CAGRs
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: GAAP BVPS CAGRs are dominated by AOCI and are not earnings power. Reported period-end BVPS rose 20.2%/yr FY2022-FY2025 (32.73 to 56.85) while BVPS excluding AOCI rose 7.8%/yr (43.18 to 54.06) and has since stalled: +2.3% in FY2025, +0.3% in nine months of 2026. The AOCI recovery is complete (GAAP BVPS has been above the ex-AOCI figure since FY2025), so further GAAP outperformance needs new rate gains rather than a rebound. Excluding cumulative currency remeasurement as well, book per share fell 4.5% year to date (42.66 to 40.73). Revenue CAGRs (-3.6%/-5.0%) are negative on USD/JPY translation; EPS CAGRs are near zero because FY2025 GAAP EPS (6.82) was depressed by investment losses against adjusted EPS of 7.49. bvps_5yr_cagr and bvps_8yr_cagr_post_split are carried from the prior version on its weighted-average-share basis (no new fiscal year has closed).
historical_growth.note_dividend_drag: Unlike FRFHF (where the projected BVPS growth rate is set GROSS of the dividend, i.e. total value creation, and the $15/share payout is then subtracted each year in the compounding formula before the dividend is separately discounted), the AFL bvps_growth_rates below are applied directly to the raw historical CAGRs, which are themselves NET of dividend already (reported shareholders equity/BVPS falls by the dividend paid, same as any company). The dividend per share is discounted as a separate cash flow to shareholders WITHOUT subtracting it again from the compounding BVPS path — subtracting it twice would double-count roughly a 4%/yr drag (current dividend yield on BVPS is $2.44/$59.96 = 4.1%) and understate intrinsic value. This is a deliberate deviation from the FRFHF file`s formula, made because AFL`s ~35-40% payout ratio (vs FRFHF`s near-100%-of-book-growth flat $15 dividend) makes the gross-up convention a much larger, harder-to-calibrate assumption here; net-of-dividend is the more conservative, better-grounded choice given the historical data available.
historical_growth.note_split: FY2015 BVPS ($40.88) is pre-2-for-1-split and not comparable to post-split figures; excluded from all CAGR calculations above.

base.description: BVPS growth of 5.0% in Year 1 and 5.5% thereafter (was 11/10/9/8.5/8). Year 1 matches the observed run rate: GAAP BVPS rose 3.9% in the first nine months of 2026 (56.85 to 59.08, ~5.2% annualised) while BVPS excluding AOCI was flat (54.06 to 54.21) and BVPS excluding AOCI and currency remeasurement fell 4.5% (42.66 to 40.73). Later years rest on the capital arithmetic rather than on the 2023-25 AOCI recovery: ~13% adjusted ROE on GAAP equity, less a ~4% dividend, less buybacks of ~5% of shares a year at ~2.1x book (which REDUCE book per share by ~5-6 points of equity for a 5-point share-count cut) gives ~3.5% before any AOCI or currency gain; 5.5% allows for rising ROE as equity shrinks, the JGB reinvestment-yield tailwind, and a modest slowing of buybacks as RBC (~575%) and holding-company liquidity ($2.7B) tighten. UNCHANGED: dividend path (the $0.61 quarterly rate was confirmed by the Q4 2026 declaration), exit P/B 2.0x, cost of equity 9.0%. Cross-check: Year-5 value of ~$154 is ~15x an adjusted EPS of ~$10.3 (7.6 compounding at ~6%/yr).

bull.description: BVPS growth 9/9/8.5/8/8 (was 14/13/12/11/10): the 2023-24 pace of book growth excluding AOCI (+10-11%/yr) roughly persists as JGB yields keep rising, Japan sales recover from the 2026 cyber-related pause, U.S. premium growth reaches the top of the 3-6% range and the Bermuda reinsurance program keeps releasing capital. The prior path implied a Year-5 price of ~$243, about 24x forward adjusted EPS, which no evidence in the filings supports. UNCHANGED: dividend path, exit P/B 2.3x, cost of equity 8.5%.

bear.description: Year-1 BVPS growth cut to 2.0% (was 5.0%): Q3 2026 showed how a single quarter of investment losses ($1.1B) takes book per share backwards, and the bear adds a cyber litigation/remediation charge across two breaches (U.S. MDL plus the June 2026 Aflac Life Japan incident under an FSA reporting order). Years 2-5 UNCHANGED at 4.5/4/4/4/4, as are the dividend path, exit P/B 1.5x and cost of equity 10.0%.

scenario_narratives.base: Book per share excluding AOCI has stopped growing (flat year to date) because Aflac returns more than it earns and buys stock at about twice book; GAAP BVPS still rises on rates and rising ROE. BVPS compounds from $59.08 to ~$76.85 by Year 5; exit at 2.0x book, about 15x forward adjusted earnings.
scenario_narratives.bull: The JGB reinvestment tailwind steepens, Japan sales recover after the 2026 cyber pause, U.S. premium growth re-accelerates and Bermuda cessions keep funding buybacks without capital strain. BVPS reaches ~$88.83 by Year 5; exit at 2.3x book.
scenario_narratives.bear: More investment losses and a material charge from the two cybersecurity incidents stall book growth in Year 1; yen weakness, Japan's demographic ceiling and tighter RBC/holding-company liquidity slow buybacks. BVPS grows to only ~$70.84 by Year 5; the multiple de-rates to 1.5x book.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: UNCHANGED at 25/50/25. The bear keeps 25% because the tail risks have multiplied rather than cleared since September: a second cybersecurity incident (Aflac Life Japan, ~4.38M customers, FSA reporting order) on top of the unresolved U.S. class action, a $1.1B investment-loss quarter, and thinner RBC and holding-company liquidity. The base and bull paths were lowered instead of shifting weight, so the deterioration is not counted twice.
probability_weighted.band_note: House/street band collapsed: SBC is immaterial for Aflac and this per-share book-value model has no SBC add-back to differ on.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Aflac is a supplemental health/life insurer where GAAP net income, GAAP EPS, and operating/free cash flow are all poor proxies for owner earnings in any single year: net income swings on non-economic net investment losses and CECL allowances (FY2025 GAAP EPS $6.82 vs management's own record adjusted EPS of $7.49), and reported shareholders' equity carries AOCI mark-to-market on a large yen-denominated JGB and USD fixed-income book that swings with interest rates independent of underlying franchise value (BVPS fell 46% in FY2021 on rate mechanics alone). This model therefore compounds BVPS per share forward at a scenario growth rate (set from the capital arithmetic: adjusted ROE less the dividend less buybacks made at about twice book, which reduce book per share even as they lift EPS), adds back the dividend, applies an exit price-to-book multiple anchored to the post-2022 AOCI-stabilized trading range (2.05x-2.37x), and discounts dividends plus the Year-5 terminal value at a cost of equity — never WACC, since net debt is held at zero throughout (the balance sheet funds policy reserves, not operating leverage to net off).
key_risks_to_valuation: Yen/dollar translation: >50% of earnings originate in Japan; sustained yen weakness mechanically depresses USD-reported BVPS growth and dividends even if yen-denominated economics are unchanged
AOCI/interest-rate sensitivity: a renewed decline in JGB or U.S. rates would compress reported BVPS via unrealized bond losses, independent of the underlying insurance business

Two cybersecurity incidents in twelve months: the June 2025 U.S. breach (~22.65M individuals; class action proceeding after an August 2026 motion-to-dismiss denial) and the June 2026 Aflac Life Japan breach (~4.38M customers; FSA reporting order, ~$40M cost and a Q3 sales pause). Litigation and remediation cost is sized only in the bear's Year 1

Exit multiple risk: the entire post-2022 P/B anchor range (2.05x-2.37x) reflects a period of rising/high rates improving reinvestment yields; a return to a near-zero-rate regime could compress the sustainable multiple below the bear case's 1.5x floor

Japan demographic decline structurally caps the core cancer/medical addressable market, requiring continual costly product renewal (Miraito, Onsen Tallett, Tsumitasu) just to sustain flat-to-growing sales

Capital return exceeds earnings: nine-month 2026 buybacks ($2.8B) plus dividends ran ahead of net earnings ($2.1B) while combined RBC slipped to ~575% and holding-company liquidity to $2.7B; a forced slowdown removes the main driver of per-share growth

Model limit: a constant exit P/B on slow-growing book understates value if buybacks keep lifting ROE, and overstates it if the Bermuda reinsurance capital release proves hard to repeat (management has said later trades will be harder)
